name: AMD Composable Kernel (CK)
repo: ROCm/rocm-libraries (projects/composablekernel); the standalone ROCm/composable_kernel repo is a deprecated read-only mirror
production_evidence: AITER, AMD's production inference kernel library, has Composable Kernel as one of its backends alongside Triton and hand-tuned ASM (see flops/amd-rocm-aiter-kernels)
vLLM's ROCm attention and MLP paths reach CK through AITER on MI300-series parts
strengths: Built on HIP C++, so the same headers target AMD GPUs and CPUs - AMD's own framing is 'across multiple architectures including GPUs and CPUs'
CK-Tile models the hardware instead of approximating it: separate documentation for intrawave and interwave scheduling, which is the CDNA-specific decision a CUDA port cannot inherit
Header-only C++ templates: no build step, no DSL to learn, and full control at the register and shared-memory level
Ships inside the ROCm super-repo, so it versions with the rest of ROCm rather than as a separate download
weaknesses: Category honesty: CK is not a compiler and not a DSL - it is a header library, which is why compilation_strategy is template-instantiation and autotuning is false
C++ templates mean longer compile times and much worse error messages than a DSL
Written against one vendor's wavefront and matrix-core model; nothing here ports to NVIDIA
The standalone repo carries a [DEPRECATED] banner pointing at ROCm/rocm-libraries, so older docs and CI snippets that clone it are following a mirror
The user's CDNA-generation matrix is narrower than CK's: CK supports CDNA3 and CDNA4, and the existing gotcha aiter-gate-skips-rdna3-gfx1100 shows what happens on the generations in between
notes: AMD's answer to CUTLASS, and the direct counterpart to the existing cutlass-cute record - same shape (header C++ template library, template-instantiation, no autotuner), different silicon underneath. Reading the two records side by side is the point: CK-Tile's documentation is organised around intrawave versus interwave scheduling and tile structure sized to the tensor core units, where CUTLASS/CuTe is organised around warp-level MMA and CuTe layouts. That difference is the concrete content of 'porting CUDA to ROCm is not a recompile'. autotuning is false as a property of CK itself. The autotuning in the ROCm inference path happens one layer up, in AITER, which selects among CK, Triton and hand-tuned ASM - so a reader should not read AITER's measured speedups as CK's autotuning. input_languages carries cutlass-cpp because that is the schema's existing term for a C++-template kernel library and CK is the AMD instance of that shape; strictly it is HIP C++ headers rather than CUTLASS headers, and that mismatch is a vocabulary limitation rather than a claim that CK consumes CUTLASS. No compile-time figure is asserted: CK is header-only, so 'compile time' is C++ template instantiation time inside the consumer's build, which is not a per-kernel number this field can hold.
